excluded.reconciliation_note: The 10 files are the 9 excluded run transcripts plus pilot-results.md, the scoring writeup for them. Verified 30 August 2026.
excluded.reason: Design-phase pilot, Case A on Claude, all three arms. protocol.md:23 excludes pilot runs from the pre-registered grid.

retired.reason: The published 54-run grid pooled nine pilot runs that the protocol excluded.

arms.label: Question only
arms.note: The frozen prompt only. One turn. If the model asks questions they are not answered.

arms.label: All facts
arms.note: The frozen prompt with the full fact sheet appended in the first message. One turn. Equal information to the loaded condition.

arms.label: Loaded method
arms.note: The frozen method file, then the frozen prompt. The model interrogates; the operator answers only from the fact sheet and replies 'That has not been assessed' to anything off-sheet.

checks.label: Asked before answering
checks.definitional_note: Arms A and B are single-turn by construction (protocol.md:9-10), so neither can pass this check. The zero restates the design of the test.

checks.label: Real options incl. do-nothing, compared on criteria
checks.page_label: Compared real options, including doing nothing
checks.caveat: The scorer calls this the load-bearing check of the three. A more lenient reading of 'compared on criteria' credits further all-facts runs. That reading was recorded internally and is disclosed here for the first time.

checks.label: Named an untested constraint or assumption
checks.adjudication: Original scoring upheld. The re-score read the all-facts condition as 13 of 15.

checks.label: Stated kill criteria
checks.page_label: Stated what would change the call
checks.adjudication: Original scoring overturned. The question-only condition moves from 12 to 15, in the baseline's favour. This check does not discriminate between conditions.

checks.label: Surfaced the hidden decision by integrating the facts
checks.definitional_note: The hidden decision in each case turns on three facts placed in the fact sheet. None appears in the frozen prompt, which is identical across all three arms. A single-turn condition that receives only the prompt cannot obtain them. All three case files were checked. The zero restates the design of the test and is not a measurement of baseline judgement.
checks.adjudication: Original scoring upheld on both cells. The re-score read them as 5 of 15 and 15 of 15, and was found to have collapsed the MET and PARTIAL distinction the rubric calls the core of the benchmark.

checks.label: Recommendation direction matched the sealed key
Caught the planted inconsistency or bias
checks.definitional_note: The planted tension sits in the fact sheet, which the question-only condition never receives. Part of this figure is therefore an artefact of the design in the same way as the check above, though not wholly, since some of each case's tension is visible in the frozen prompt. The proportion has not been quantified.
checks.adjudication: Original scoring overturned. The question-only condition moves from 5 to 6, in the baseline's favour.

composite.label: Produced a defensible brief, on every run
composite.provenance: The lowest of the five process check counts. That is an upper bound on the number of runs that passed all five, and on this grid it equals the conjunction exactly, because every cell in it is either zero or the full fifteen. Per-run results are not published, so the conjunction itself cannot be recomputed from this page. Not an independent ninth result, and not the pre-registered headline. This line previously described the calculation as a logical AND, which is not what the code performs.
composite.recomputed_note: Recomputed over the four remaining checks the figures do not move, because the question-only condition compared real options in 0 of 15 runs and the all-facts condition tagged its evidence in 0 of 15. This recomputation was done after the fact and was not pre-registered.

go_case.label: Case B, Larkfield: moved toward the aggressive, evidence-backed call
go_case.note: The anti-hedging test. n=6 per arm, two models, three runs each. Unaffected by the pilot exclusion.

direction_by_case.note: Check c7, split by case. Published for the first time.
direction_by_case.reading: Outside Case B, direction did not discriminate between a short question and the loaded file at all. The whole measured direction deficit sits in Case B, and those question-only runs were contaminated.

legs.caveat: The scope of the 9 July rollout is not settled. OpenAI's forum post for that date uses trusted-partner language while its X post describes a broad release. The source is the X post, quoted, because openai.com returned 403.
Anthropic newsroom, opened directly. No ambiguity on this leg.

hashed_inputs.note: The six frozen inputs, hashed before the first scored run. Values transcribed from PREREGISTRATION.md at the pre-registration commit and verified against it.
hashed_inputs.product_withheld_note: The product file is deliberately not published; only its hash is. That hash proves nothing to a reader who does not hold the file. What it does is let anyone who has a copy confirm that theirs is the version benchmarked here.

inventory.pilot_note: Nine excluded run transcripts plus pilot-results.md, the scoring writeup for them.

transcripts.withdrawn_note: The two transcript excerpts previously shown here are withdrawn. One tagged a figure DERIVED where the case file supplies it directly, which under the product's own scheme makes it GIVEN, and the case file is one click away. The replacement will show the model integrating a fact it obtained by asking, rather than restating one it was given.

answering_rule.text: The answering rule (Arm C) is fixed and published so the interrogation phase is reproducible and the operator cannot feed the model convenient answers. Off-sheet questions are answered "That has not been assessed" so that how each condition handles a genuine unknown is itself measured.

substrate.text: Vanilla conditions: ChatGPT and Gemini verified to have no custom instructions; Claude custom style set to Normal for the run window, then restored (the restoration is logged). API with an empty system prompt is the preferred clean substrate if keys are available; browser automation is the fallback.

protocol_quotes.substrate_actual: Browser automation was the fallback used. The transcript header for the contaminated runs records the platform as chatgpt.com in a temporary chat under browser automation.

case_design.text: The three cases are fictional and cannot be found through search.

parity.statement: Arm B carries equal information to Arm C; the only difference is the product's discipline. The pre-registration names it the sceptic's controlled comparison. In Arm C the operator answers each question using only the fact sheet, verbatim in substance, and replies 'That has not been assessed' to anything off-sheet, so the operator cannot feed the model convenient answers.

deviations.title: The composite is not the pre-registered headline
deviations.detail: rubric-operationalisations.md:23 pre-registers checks 6 and 7 as the primary result, and rubric:3 states a run's score is a vector, not a single number. Leading with a Group 1 composite is a primary-endpoint substitution.

deviations.title: Pilot runs were pooled and the promise not to pool them was deleted afterwards
deviations.detail: protocol.md:23 excluded them, and still does. Commit 85f8c71, 14 July 2026, deleted the matching sentence from PREREGISTRATION.md and set that record to COMMITTED. Scoring finished 6 July 2026, eight days earlier. The original wording survives in commit 1dfeb6d. This page reports only the 45 pre-registered runs. The attribution in this entry was itself corrected on 11 August 2026: it previously named protocol.md as the file edited.

deviations.title: The published pre-registration commit ID does not exist
deviations.detail: 5e89de4842693444c27e893470efecb242486cd2 is in no ref. The real commit is 3e5e46f1a7cc154e1b91120ec9336e3eb089fd2c. Anyone who followed the published verification procedure failed at step 1, and the failure would have looked like their own mistake.

deviations.title: No transcript is published
deviations.detail: protocol.md:34 commits that every published count is traceable to a downloadable transcript. None is.

deviations.title: The sealed reference answers are not published
deviations.detail: Every adjudicated cell was settled against a key nobody outside can read. Its SHA-256 was verified against the pre-registration table and that check cannot be repeated while the file is withheld.

deviations.title: Transcripts were not de-identified before scoring
deviations.detail: Contrary to protocol.md:27. The sole scorer was the operator who ran the grid. Every filename carries its condition and model, and each carries an operator note stating the verdict.

deviations.title: The original scoring was mildly biased toward widening the gap
deviations.detail: Stricter than the rubric text inside Arm A, looser inside Arm B. Two cells were overturned on adjudication and both ran that way, both in the baseline's favour.

deviations.title: The single-scorer cross-check was never run
deviations.detail: protocol.md:30 makes an LLM cross-check the condition of falling back to one scorer. The fallback happened and the cross-check did not.

deviations.title: Baseline partial-pass counts are not published
deviations.detail: protocol.md:31 requires them prominently, per case, and the rubric calls the full-versus-partial distinction the core of the benchmark.

deviations.title: The rubric set no integration threshold
deviations.detail: Both scoring passes invented one and disagreed. The rule is now pre-committed: two of three facts with the third absent scores PARTIAL.

deviations.title: The published rationale for the one near-miss overstates it
deviations.detail: The record says two of three facts were integrated. The adjudication found one.

deviations.title: The sharpest discriminators in the sealed key went unused
deviations.detail: The Case C falsification element and the explicit NOT clauses in both cases were applied by neither scoring pass.

deviations.title: The GO case was published with the informed baseline removed
deviations.detail: The site showed 0 of 6 against 6 of 6 and omitted the middle column, which is also 6 of 6.

deviations.title: The case where the file adds least was never identified
deviations.detail: protocol.md:36 requires it. It is Case B, Larkfield.

deviations.title: Per-case, per-condition counts are not published
deviations.detail: The rubric names them as the headline unit. Direction is now split by case; the other seven checks are not.

deviations.title: The alternative reading of the options check was kept internal
deviations.detail: A more lenient reading credits further all-facts runs on the check the scorer calls load-bearing.

deviations.title: The question-only condition was contaminated on Case B
deviations.detail: ChatGPT invoked live web search unprompted during those runs. Those six runs carry the whole of the direction deficit reported anywhere on this site.

deviations.title: The 14-day refresh commitment lapsed
deviations.detail: No date-stamped history was published. The dates and the arithmetic are in the status section.

clean: Six inputs were hashed and frozen before the first scored run, and all six SHA-256 values match their files when read with LF line endings.

The reduction in planned sample size from the pre-registered target of 180 runs is logged exactly as the protocol required, at both steps: first to 54 runs, then to the current 45 when the nine design-phase pilot runs were removed.
limitations: No condition in this grid resembles a real operator. The question-only condition has nothing and the all-facts condition has everything. An operator who arrives with most of what matters and a blind spot they cannot see is the condition the product exists for, and it was not run.

One person ran the grid, scored it, held the sealed reference answers, and answered the file's questions during the runs. The re-score was carried out by three agents working from the published rubric, blind to the original scoring. Neither they nor the adjudication were independent of GreenSquare AI, and this page does not use that word.
Two published cells are definitional rather than empirical, and a third is partly so. A single-turn condition cannot ask before answering, and it cannot obtain three facts that are not in its prompt.

The three checks that separate most cleanly are the behaviours the file instructs the model to perform. A reasonable reading is that they measure whether the file was loaded, not whether the model reasoned better.
The all-facts condition was not information-equal between the two models on Case B. The Claude fact sheet carries two cross-reference pointers the ChatGPT one lacks.
n is 15 per condition, three repeats per cell. The grid is small and unbalanced, with Case A running on one model only.

The run inventory reconciles. Both directory counts were verified on disk, 45 grid transcripts and 10 pilot files, and the arithmetic requires 9. The tenth file was opened on 30 August 2026: it is the scoring writeup for the nine excluded pilot runs, and it states in its own opening paragraph that they are not pooled with the pre-registered grid. This entry previously reported the inventory as unreconciled and the tenth file as unopened.
What was tested is a file fixed by its published hash. Nothing here commits any later release to being that same file.
